core.text: Hypothesis: agitation creates transient optical disturbance; failed optical checks command further agitation, renewing disturbance. The rival account attributes failed checks to unresolved dye gradients. Only the rule and image fluctuations are stipulated; operation of this reinforcing loop is unobserved.

Propose three fresh paired comparisons within six trials, alternating pair order. Hold the 150 mL water/0.30 mL dye demand, bottle, addition location, camera and commanded 900 rpm fixed. Enable the optical stop rule in one trial; sever its command return link in the other by stopping at second 60 while logging the rule in shadow mode. Stop every trial by second 105. This manipulates feedback authority, with duration as its consequence.

Sample three elevations beginning at second 120, alternate sampling order, and report raw attenuation, normalized spread, stop times and every failure. The stipulated 300 rpm result already met the 4 percent proxy once. Success of the proposed 900 rpm timer intervention remains hypothetical; side-image stability cannot substitute for samples.

residue.text: Record shadow failures at the imposed stop and matched images before and after cessation. Hypothetically, promptly falling spread with reduced stirring and successful final vials would support an agitation-to-image effect plus dispensable optical commands. A timer stop alone cannot establish that feedback actually prolonged the enabled run.

Timer and enabled trials can differ in quiet time before sampling; record this confound. Sampling disturbance, unverified rpm and absent concentration calibration constrain attribution. Specks remain unidentified, and image changes could reflect surface shape or settling. Equal final success would establish bounded feedback dispensability in these trials, without proving the disturbance mechanism.

Retain spill-tray protection and stop on escaping liquid. Both arms failing, unchanged stirring duration, or inconsistent replicates leave the comparison unresolved. No extrapolation to other materials, scales or continuous operation is established.

tension.account_a: Hypothesis: renewed agitation-induced optical disturbance sustains unnecessary feedback commands after the sample proxy is achievable.
tension.account_b: Rival hypothesis: genuine gradients cause failed checks, and their commanded additional stirring is needed to meet the sample proxy in this comparison.
tension.prediction_a: With initial demand fixed, severed trials would stop despite shadow-rule failures; enabled trials would stir longer, yet both would meet the final 4 percent target. Rapid image improvement after externally imposed cessation would provide additional, non-identifying support.
tension.prediction_b: Under the same comparison, severed trials would exceed 4 percent final-vial spread while longer enabled trials would meet it. This would favor useful additional mixing, subject to differing quiet times, without establishing necessity of 900 rpm or this rule.
